problem: A V17 DONE terminal receipt is source-idempotent and uniquely bound, but repeated reads of that valid receipt can still drive the current mutable RewardPlasticityCandidate more than once. A separate consumption ledger would not be sufficient while reward state itself is persisted outside the same UnifiedDB transaction.
hypothesis: Treat the unique producer-owned V17 DONE receipt set as source truth and reward state as a deterministic rebuildable projection. Canonically scan unique terminal receipts, re-adjudicate each through the non-bypassable terminal reward bridge, sort by a versioned deterministic order, and fold into a fresh RewardState. Retry/restart/cache loss then cannot accumulate duplicate learning because no mutable per-read consume operation exists.
ordinary_discriminator: authoritative DONE universe is scanned without caller-supplied effect list
explicit_no_learning remains visible but does not mutate material reward state
two separate Python process replays must reconstruct identical state and learned-set/order digests
raw mutable plasticity is an explicit negative control and must double-learn the same admitted evidence
process hard-exits after fsync of a derived cache; retry must rebuild identically
a deliberately corrupted derived cache must be ignored
one new unique terminal receipt must add exactly one material event
replaying after that addition must not add another event
deleting one source DONE receipt on disposable state must change the projection, exposing source-lineage rollback as a hard unresolved dependency
strongest_counterhypothesis: A mutable RewardConsumptionReceipt can be preferable for incremental O(1)-ish updates, but it is only correctness-sufficient if consumption metadata and the authoritative persistent reward-state mutation share one atomic transaction or if reward state is itself explicitly derived and independently verifiable. A ledger plus an external JSON reward state leaves a crash/ack split-brain window.
external_mechanism_basis: SQLite official atomic-commit/transaction documentation: atomicity applies to changes in the same transactional database operation; it does not make a separately persisted JSON state atomic with a UnifiedDB consumption row.
Event-sourcing literature and 2026 agent event-log work motivate immutable source events plus deterministic rebuildable projections, but do not prove this Frank implementation or its performance.
hard_limits: source-lineage rollback/replacement is not solved by the fold and remains F-V01-13/UnifiedDB authority
reward dimension/utility policy remains test-only TASK binary mapping
full replay cost is O(number of terminal receipts) unless a verified derived materialization/cache frontier is added
no whole F-V01-11 or Frank v0.1 promotion
